name: Timemage cuts the duration of harmful magic auras on the Chronomancer by 30% (#3656)
contract: Timemage 806753 is a passive whose only effect is SPELL_AURA_MOD_AURA_DURATION_BY_DISPEL (245) with EffectMiscValue 1 = DISPEL_MAGIC and EffectBasePoints -31, resolving to -30 with DieSides 1. Unit::ModSpellDuration consumes it as target->GetTotalAuraModifierByMiscValue(SPELL_AURA_MOD_AURA_DURATION_BY_DISPEL, spellProto->Dispel) followed by AddPct(duration, durationMod) (Unit.cpp), inside the 'if (!positive)' branch that exists to cut the duration of negative effects only; 'target' is the unit receiving the aura, which is the Chronomancer, matching the tooltip's 'on you'. Spell::ApplyAura calls it with positive taken from the aura application's own flag (Spell.cpp). The fixture debuff is Enlarged 84003: Dispel 1 (magic), Attributes 0x2C000000 including SPELL_ATTR0_AURA_IS_DEBUFF, which makes SpellInfo::_IsPositiveEffect return false for every effect, so AuraApplication::_InitFlags marks the self-cast application negative; both its effects are EffectImplicitTargetA 1 (TARGET_UNIT_CASTER), so SpellInfo::CheckExplicitTarget needs no hostile target; DurationIndex 25 is a flat 180000 ms with no per-level scaling; its mechanic mask is empty, so GetDiminishingReturnsGroupForSpell returns DIMINISHING_NONE and no diminishing cap interferes. A self-cast is the harness's only way to land a harmful aura on a player, since there is no player-versus-player combat here; Unit::ModSpellDuration reaches the same branch either way ('xinef: also calculate self casts'). 180000 ms becomes 126000 ms with the talent. Native handlers only. Regression scenario for behaviour that already works.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Talented Chronomancer takes the same debuff
The debuff lands on the control
The debuff lands on the talented Chronomancer
Without the talent the debuff keeps its full 180 second duration
With the talent the same debuff is cut to 126 seconds
